tagline: What satellites can and cannot see

zones.name: Ica Valley
zones.description: Long-established irrigated valley floor of the Ica River.
zones.mask: cropland (annual max NDVI > 0.4 in any year 2020-2024)

zones.name: Villacurí plains
zones.description: Desert plains north-west of Ica, irrigated mostly with groundwater.
zones.mask: cropland (annual max NDVI > 0.4 in any year 2020-2024)

zones.name: Desert control
zones.description: Hyper-arid desert with no irrigation, used to remove the shared climate signal.
zones.mask: never-green desert (annual max NDVI < 0.12 every year 2004-2024)

zones.name: Ica-Villacurí water block
zones.description: Both irrigated zones together; the smallest area coarse water products can speak to.

zones.name: Upper Ica basin
zones.description: Andean headwaters (above 2,500 m) where the rain that recharges the aquifer falls.
zones.mask: elevation above 2,500 m (SRTM) inside the HydroBASINS level-7 Ica basin

zones.name: Central Valley, California
zones.description: Comparison case: California's Sacramento and San Joaquin valleys, where irrigation pumps far more groundwater than in Ica and GRACE first measured aquifer depletion from space.

zones.name: High Plains (Ogallala), United States

zones.mask: none (box 104.5°W-96.5°W, 32.0°N-43.5°N; approximate, not the official aquifer boundary)

zones.name: Northwest India (Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan)
zones.description: Rice and wheat irrigated from wells; the region where GRACE first showed large groundwater loss in India.

zones.description: Wheat and maize fields and large cities drawing on deep and shallow aquifers.

wells.note: Each rate compares the first and last static level of a well; there is no monthly series, so no significance test is run on wells.

impact.overdraft_source: Salmoral et al. (2020), Reconciling irrigation demands for agricultural expansion with environmental sustainability: A preliminary assessment for the Ica Valley, Peru. Journal of Cleaner Production 276, 123544, doi:10.1016/j.jclepro.2020.123544
impact.irrigated_area_note: Cropland pixels (yearly peak NDVI > 0.4 in 2020-2024) inside the Ica Valley and Villacurí zones.
impact.et_note: MODIS MOD16A2GF evapotranspiration times cropland area. Rain is close to zero here, so this is water supplied by irrigation (groundwater and, in the Ica Valley, also river water). MOD16 tends to underestimate ET on irrigated fields, so these volumes are lower bounds.
impact.note: Detection time from Weatherhead et al. (1998) with GRACE's own noise and memory, assuming the overdraft were the only change. A rough lower bound, not a forecast.

atlas.name: Ica-Villacurí, Peru
atlas.description: Both irrigated zones together; the smallest area coarse water products can speak to.
atlas.reading: Its cropland is getting greener and using more water (MODIS). GRACE sees stored water rising. Yet 69% of monitored wells are falling: the farms are too small for one GRACE footprint, so the satellites cannot localise the loss.

atlas.name: Central Valley, California
atlas.description: Comparison case: California's Sacramento and San Joaquin valleys, where irrigation pumps far more groundwater than in Ica and GRACE first measured aquifer depletion from space.
atlas.reading: GRACE sees stored water falling. Rain shows no proven decline, so the loss points to groundwater pumping.

atlas.name: High Plains (Ogallala), United States
atlas.description: Irrigated grain belt over the Ogallala aquifer, from South Dakota to Texas.
atlas.reading: GRACE sees stored water falling. Rain shows no proven decline, so the loss points to groundwater pumping.
atlas.reference: Richey et al. (2015); Rodell et al. (2018)

atlas.name: Guarani aquifer system, South America
atlas.description: One of the world's largest aquifers, under Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina and Uruguay, in a humid region.
atlas.reading: Its cropland is getting greener (MODIS). No proven change in stored water from space. A change this size would need about 51 years of data to show up.

atlas_note: Boxes around each aquifer system are approximate, not official aquifer boundaries. Same NASA products, period (2004-2024) and engine everywhere; only El Niño (ONI) is used as a control outside Ica.

demo_cases.title: The greening desert
demo_cases.text: Villacurí's desert plains turned green as irrigated fields spread. Is the trend real, and is it irrigation or just a few rainy years?

demo_cases.title: The invisible drop
demo_cases.text: Wells in the Ica valley keep dropping. Can NASA's water satellites see it from space?

demo_cases.title: The cooling oasis
demo_cases.text: The region's air is warming, yet Villacurí's fields keep getting cooler. How can both be true?

demo_cases.title: The false alarm
demo_cases.text: A classic trend test says Ica's groundwater is rising, with p = 0.000004. Our engine cross-examines that claim.
